question: Tennis and squash players carry extra bone in the hitting arm. When does starting the sport roughly double that gain?
answer: Before or around puberty. Kannus and colleagues compared the two arms of female national-level players: those who began before or around their first period had two to three times the side-to-side difference of those who began later. Growing bone can widen as well as densify, and a wider tube resists bending far better.
move: The same effort buys most while the thing is still being built.
ask: What effort would pay off most if I started it now, while I am still growing?
trap: Assuming bone answers exercise about equally well at any age.
source: Kannus et al., Annals of Internal Medicine, 1995
reference: Kannus et al., Effect of starting age of physical activity on bone mass in the dominant arm of tennis and squash players, Annals of Internal Medicine, 1995
